{{family name hatnote|Aida|lang=Japanese}}
{{nihongo|'''Aida Yasuaki'''|会田 安明||February 10, 1747 – October 26, 1817}} also known as '''Aida Ammei''', was a Japanese [[mathematician]] in the [[Edo period]].<ref>Smith, David. (1914). {{Google books|J1YNAAAAYAAJ|''A History of Japanese Mathematics,'' p. 188. |page=188}}</ref>

He made significant contributions to the fields of [[number theory]] and [[geometry]], and furthered methods for simplifying [[continued fractions]].

Aida created an original symbol for "equal".  This was the first appearance of the notation for equal in East Asia.<ref name="jochi38">Jochi, Shigeru. (1997). {{Google books|raKRY3KQspsC&dq|"Aida, Yasuaki," ''Encyclopaedia of the History of Science, Technology, and Medicine in Non-Western Cultures,'' p. 38. |page=38}}</ref>
